_comment: Coyolxauhqui Ridge Solar Observatory vuln-planting side. Every new catalog config referenced here is GENERIC and var-driven (see boxbuilder/vulndb_vuln_configs/): uid0-user, loosen-file-mode, insecure-file-mode, local-user, user-login-shell, user-sudo-nopasswd, systemd-service, pam-permit-auth, apache-site -- all theme detail lives in the vars below, not in the catalog rows, so any future box reuses the same seeds. loosen-file-mode (chmod only, no content write) is used for /etc/shadow and /etc/passwd; insecure-file-mode (rewrites content) is only for files we create. loosen-file-mode for /etc/shadow and /etc/passwd MUST run after every account-creation/shell step (uid0-user, local-user, user-login-shell) -- useradd/usermod/chpasswd rewrite those files and reset their mode on the way out (0666 decays to 0664), so chmod-ing first gets silently undone; confirmed the hard way on the 149 round. Each FILE_PATH / SERVICE_NAME / USERNAME here MUST match its paired check's collect.path / service / username in solar-observatory.scenario.yaml exactly -- nothing cross-checks them. uplink-relay and mirror-fan are ALSO scored by a `process_state` check (collect.pattern is a regex matched against /proc/<pid>/cmdline), which is why each needs a distinctively-named EXEC_START/PAYLOAD_PATH (mirror-fan runs PAYLOAD_PATH=/usr/local/sbin/mirror-fanctl instead of a bland `sleep`) rather than a launcher whose cmdline is generic -- if you rename either payload path, update the matching `collect.pattern` in solar-observatory.scenario.yaml too. `ssh-root-login` comes from the shared vulndb catalog (no local seed). Run `nakon catalog check --config solar-observatory.nakon.json --json` after the bundled seeds have been ensured in vulndb.
